import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.26

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The *ordinal height* of a variety of groups is, by definition, the supremum of the
order types (ordinals) of all chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered
by inclusion. It is clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite,
or equal to $\omega_1$. Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some
variety?

A variety of groups is understood in the sense of Birkhoff and Neumann: a class of
groups closed under homomorphic images, subgroups and (unrestricted) direct products,
or equivalently the class of all groups satisfying a given set of laws (words in the
free group on countably many generators). Groups are taken with underlying type in
`Type`, so classes of groups live in `Type 1` and ordinal heights in `Ordinal.{1}`.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Springer, 1967.
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/-- A class of groups: a predicate on groups whose underlying type lives in `Type`.
Classes are ordered by inclusion, so `W < V` means that `W` is a proper subclass of `V`. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type 1 := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- A class of groups `V` is a *variety* if it is closed under homomorphic images
(in particular under isomorphism), under subgroups and under unrestricted direct
products (including the empty product, so `V` contains the trivial group).
By Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups defined by a set of laws. -/
structure IsVariety (V : GroupClass) : Prop where
  /-- `V` is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective : ∀ {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Surjective f → V G → V H
  /-- `V` is closed under subgroups. -/
  subgroup : ∀ {G : Type} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), V G → V H
  /-- `V` is closed under unrestricted direct products. -/
  pi : ∀ {ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, V (G i)) → V (∀ i, G i)

/-- A chain of proper subvarieties of the class `V` that is well-ordered by inclusion:
a set of varieties, each strictly contained in `V`, on which strict inclusion is a
well-order. -/
structure WellOrderedChain (V : GroupClass) where
  /-- The members of the chain. -/
  carrier : Set GroupClass
  /-- Every member of the chain is a variety. -/
  isVariety : ∀ W ∈ carrier, IsVariety W
  /-- Every member of the chain is a proper subclass of `V`. -/
  lt : ∀ W ∈ carrier, W < V
  /-- The chain is well-ordered by inclusion. -/
  isWellOrder : IsWellOrder carrier (· < ·)

/-- The *ordinal height* of a class of groups `V`: the supremum of the order types of all
chains of proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered by inclusion. -/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupClass) : Ordinal.{1} :=
  ⨆ c : WellOrderedChain V, @Ordinal.type c.carrier (· < ·) c.isWellOrder

/-- The class of all groups is a variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isVariety_top : IsVariety ⊤ where
  of_surjective _ _ _ := trivial
  subgroup _ _ := trivial
  pi _ := trivial

/-- The class of trivial groups is a variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isVariety_subsingleton : IsVariety fun G _ => Subsingleton G where
  of_surjective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  subgroup _ _ := inferInstance
  pi _ := inferInstance

/-- Every variety contains all trivial groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsVariety.subsingleton_le {V : GroupClass} (hV : IsVariety V) :
    (fun G _ => Subsingleton G) ≤ V := by
  intro G _ hG
  have h : V (∀ i : Empty, (fun _ => G) i) := hV.pi fun i => i.elim
  exact hV.of_surjective (1 : (∀ i : Empty, (fun _ => G) i) →* G)
    (fun g => ⟨fun i => i.elim, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩) h

/-- The trivial variety has no proper subvarieties, so its ordinal height is `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem ordinalHeight_subsingleton : ordinalHeight (fun G _ => Subsingleton G) = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm (Ordinal.iSup_le fun c => ?_) (zero_le _)
  have hempty : IsEmpty c.carrier := ⟨fun ⟨W, hW⟩ =>
    (c.lt W hW).not_ge ((c.isVariety W hW).subsingleton_le)⟩
  exact le_of_eq ((@Ordinal.type_eq_zero_iff_isEmpty c.carrier (· < ·) c.isWellOrder).2 hempty)

/--
Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety of groups?

Here the *ordinal height* of a variety is the supremum of the order types of all chains of
its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. A countable ordinal is one whose
cardinality is finite or countably infinite; in particular `0` is realised by the trivial
variety, whose only chain of proper subvarieties is the empty chain.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal.{1}, α.card ≤ ℵ₀ →
      ∃ V : GroupClass, IsVariety V ∧ ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's single slot and its notes (include finite ordinals and 0; the preceding sentences are a definition and a remark, not questions) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: A variety is defined via Birkhoff closure (homomorphic images, subgroups, unrestricted direct products) on classes of groups whose carrier type lives in `Type`; by Birkhoff's HSP theorem (valid within the universe `Type`, since free groups on sets in `Type` and all needed products stay in `Type`) this coincides with the class of groups satisfying a set of laws in `FreeGroup ℕ`, the alternative reading mentioned in the decomposition notes.

Closure under 'quotients' is stated as closure under surjective homomorphisms (homomorphic images), which also gives closure under isomorphism; closure under subgroups is stated literally with `Subgroup G`. The empty product is included, so every variety contains the trivial group and the empty class is not a variety (as in H. Neumann's book).

Classes of groups are `∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop`, so they carry the Pi order; `W < V` is strict inclusion, i.e. `W` is a proper subclass. 'Well-ordered by inclusion' is `IsWellOrder carrier (· < ·)` (linear + well-founded strict inclusion), and the order type is `Ordinal.type` of that relation.

Because classes of groups live in `Type 1`, the ordinal height is an `Ordinal.{1}` and the quantified ordinal α is in `Ordinal.{1}`; the supremum `⨆` over `WellOrderedChain V : Type 1` into `Ordinal.{1}` is bounded (`Ordinal.bddAbove_range`), hence a genuine least upper bound. The universe choice is cosmetic and does not change the mathematics.
'Countable ordinal' is rendered as `α.card ≤ ℵ₀`, which includes 0 and all finite ordinals (as the decomposition notes require) and is equivalent to `α < ω₁`.
The chain members are required to be varieties (`IsVariety W`) and proper subclasses of `V`; `V` itself is required to be a variety in the theorem, not in `ordinalHeight`.
AMS tags 3 (logic/set theory, for ordinals) and 20 (group theory) were used.

by A. V. Kuznetsov

all chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. Is
every countable ordinal the ordinal height of some variety?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/--
A variety of groups, represented by its identities in the free group on
countably many variables. The identities form a subgroup invariant under every
substitution of words for variables. Inclusion of varieties is reverse
inclusion of their identity subgroups.
-/
structure GroupVariety where
  identities : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)
  substitution_closed : ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, identities.map f ≤ identities

@[ext]
theorem GroupVariety.ext {V W : GroupVariety} (h : V.identities = W.identities) : V = W := by
  cases V
  cases W
  simp_all

instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le V W := W.identities ≤ V.identities
  le_refl _ := le_rfl
  le_trans _ _ _ hVW hWU := hWU.trans hVW
  le_antisymm V W hVW hWV := GroupVariety.ext (le_antisymm hWV hVW)

/--
The ordinal height of a group variety: the supremum of the order types of all
well-ordered chains of its proper subvarieties. An order embedding from the
canonical type of an ordinal into the strict lower interval represents such a
chain.
-/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal :=
  sSup {α : Ordinal | Nonempty (α.ToType ↪o Set.Iio V)}

/--
Is every countable ordinal number, including every finite ordinal and zero, the
ordinal height of some variety of groups? Here a variety is understood in the
Birkhoff--Neumann sense, and `ordinalHeight` is the supremum of the order types
of all inclusion-well-ordered chains of proper subvarieties.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal, α.card ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 →
      ∃ V : GroupVariety, ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»
modeling_decisions: A group variety is represented by its identity subgroup in `FreeGroup ℕ`. Closure under every endomorphism expresses closure of identities under substitutions; the order is reversed identity-subgroup inclusion, matching inclusion of the corresponding classes of groups.

A well-ordered chain of proper subvarieties is represented by an order embedding from an ordinal's canonical `ToType` into `Set.Iio V`. The height is the `sSup` of all such ordinals, so the supremum need not itself be attained by a chain.
Countable ordinals are expressed by `α.card ≤ Cardinal.aleph0`, which includes zero and all finite ordinals.

/-!

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The ordinal height of a variety of groups is the supremum of the order types
of all its chains of proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
Is every countable ordinal the ordinal height of some variety?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/-- A group satisfies a law when the corresponding word in the free group on
countably many variables evaluates to the identity under every assignment. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A variety of groups, represented canonically by its full equational theory
in the free group on countably many variables. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)
  isFullTheory : ∀ w, w ∈ laws ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ v ∈ laws, SatisfiesLaw G v) → SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- Inclusion of group varieties. Since a smaller variety satisfies more laws,
this is reverse inclusion of their full equational theories. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le V W := W.laws ⊆ V.laws
  le_refl _ := Set.Subset.rfl
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ := h₂.trans h₁
  le_antisymm V W h₁ h₂ := by
    cases V
    cases W
    simp_all only [GroupVariety.mk.injEq]
    exact Set.Subset.antisymm h₂ h₁

/-- The ordinal height of a group variety is the supremum of the order types of
its inclusion-well-ordered chains of proper subvarieties. -/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal :=
  sSup {α | ∃ C : α.ToType → GroupVariety, StrictMono C ∧ ∀ i, C i < V}

/--
Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety of groups?
Here countable ordinals are precisely the ordinals below $\omega_1$, and the
ordinal height is the supremum of the order types of all chains of proper
subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal, α < Ordinal.omega 1 →
      ∃ V : GroupVariety, ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»
modeling_decisions: A group identity is represented by a word in `FreeGroup ℕ` required to evaluate to the identity under every assignment; this captures arbitrary group equations because an equation `u = v` is equivalent to the law `u * v⁻¹ = 1`.

A group variety is represented canonically by its full semantically closed equational theory, rather than by an arbitrary presentation of laws. This identifies different presentations defining the same class of groups.
Variety inclusion is reverse inclusion of full law theories: a smaller class of groups satisfies more identities.

A well-ordered inclusion chain of order type `α` is represented by a `StrictMono` map from `α.ToType` into the proper subvarieties. The empty domain represents the empty chain, allowing ordinal height zero.
Countable ordinals are expressed as ordinals strictly below `Ordinal.omega 1`, Mathlib's first uncountable ordinal.

/-!

by A. V. Kuznetsov

types (ordinals) of all chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
It is clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite, or equal to
$\omega_1$. Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety?

A variety of groups (in the sense of Birkhoff and H. Neumann) is a class of groups closed
under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and cartesian products; equivalently, it is the
class of all groups satisfying some set of laws. Here a variety is modelled as such a class
of groups in `Type`, and varieties are ordered by inclusion.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/-- A variety of groups: a class of groups (here, of groups in `Type`) that is closed under
taking subgroups, homomorphic images and cartesian products. -/
@[ext]
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The class of groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- A variety is closed under taking subgroups (up to isomorphism). -/
  mem_of_injective {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : H →* G) :
    Function.Injective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- A variety is closed under taking homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) :
    Function.Surjective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- A variety is closed under taking cartesian products. -/
  mem_pi {ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)] :
    (∀ i, Mem (G i)) → Mem (∀ i, G i)

/-- Varieties are ordered by inclusion: `V ≤ W` iff every group in `V` lies in `W`. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le V W := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ := id
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ hG := h₂ G (h₁ G hG)
  le_antisymm V W h₁ h₂ :=
    GroupVariety.ext (funext fun G => funext fun _ => propext ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩)

/-- The set of order types of the chains of proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered
by inclusion. -/
def chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : Set Ordinal.{1} :=
  {o | ∃ (C : Set GroupVariety) (_ : IsWellOrder C (· < ·)),
    (∀ W ∈ C, W < V) ∧ Ordinal.type (α := C) (· < ·) = o}

/-- The ordinal height of a variety `V`: the supremum of the order types of all chains of
proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered by inclusion. -/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal.{1} :=
  sSup (chainOrderTypes V)

/-- The empty chain contributes the order type `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem zero_mem_chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : 0 ∈ chainOrderTypes V :=
  ⟨∅, inferInstance, fun _ h => h.elim, Ordinal.type_eq_zero_of_empty _⟩

/-- The order types of well-ordered chains of subvarieties are bounded, so `ordinalHeight` is a
genuine supremum. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem bddAbove_chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : BddAbove (chainOrderTypes V) := by
  refine ⟨(Order.succ #GroupVariety).ord, ?_⟩
  rintro o ⟨C, _, -, rfl⟩
  exact (lt_ord.2 (Order.lt_succ_iff.2 ((Ordinal.card_type _).le.trans (mk_set_le C)))).le

/-- `ordinalHeight V` is the least upper bound of the order types of the well-ordered chains of
proper subvarieties of `V`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem isLUB_ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : IsLUB (chainOrderTypes V) (ordinalHeight V) :=
  isLUB_csSup ⟨0, zero_mem_chainOrderTypes V⟩ (bddAbove_chainOrderTypes V)

/-- The trivial variety, consisting of the trivial groups. -/
def trivialVariety : GroupVariety where
  Mem G _ := Subsingleton G
  mem_of_injective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_of_surjective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_pi h := by
    haveI := h
    infer_instance

/-- Every variety contains the trivial groups, so the trivial variety is the smallest variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem trivialVariety_le (V : GroupVariety) : trivialVariety ≤ V := by
  intro G _ hG
  haveI : Subsingleton G := hG
  exact V.mem_of_surjective (1 : (∀ _ : Empty, Unit) →* G)
    (fun g => ⟨1, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩) (V.mem_pi fun i => i.elim)

/-- The trivial variety has no proper subvarieties, so its ordinal height is `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem ordinalHeight_trivialVariety : ordinalHeight trivialVariety = 0 := by
  have h : chainOrderTypes trivialVariety = {0} := by
    refine Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.2 ⟨zero_mem_chainOrderTypes _, ?_⟩
    rintro o ⟨C, _, hC, rfl⟩
    haveI : IsEmpty C := ⟨fun W => ((hC W W.2).trans_le (trivialVariety_le W)).false⟩
    exact Ordinal.type_eq_zero_of_empty _
  rw [ordinalHeight, h, csSup_singleton]

/--
The *ordinal height* of a variety of groups is the supremum of the order types (ordinals) of all
chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. Is every countable ordinal
number the ordinal height of some variety?

Here a countable ordinal is an ordinal $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| \le \aleph_0$; in particular the
finite ordinals are included.
-/

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.26

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The ordinal height of a variety of groups is the supremum of the order types of
all its chains of proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. Is
every countable ordinal the ordinal height of some variety of groups?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/--
A variety of groups, represented by its laws in the free group on countably
many variables. Its laws form a normal subgroup and are closed under every
endomorphism of the free group (that is, under every substitution of words for
variables).
-/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The group words that are laws of the variety. -/
  laws : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)
  normal_laws : laws.Normal
  fullyInvariant : ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, ∀ w ∈ laws, f w ∈ laws

/--
`U` is a proper subvariety of `V`. Inclusion is reversed on their groups of
laws: a smaller variety satisfies strictly more laws.
-/
def IsProperSubvariety (U V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  V.laws < U.laws

/--
The order types of chains of proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered
by inclusion. Such a chain is indexed by the canonical well-order of an
ordinal, and increases strictly with respect to inclusion of varieties.
-/
def ChainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : Set Ordinal.{0} :=
  {o | ∃ c : o.ToType → GroupVariety,
    (∀ i, IsProperSubvariety (c i) V) ∧
    ∀ ⦃i j⦄, i < j → IsProperSubvariety (c i) (c j)}

/--
The ordinal height of a variety: the supremum of the order types of all chains
of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
-/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal.{0} :=
  sSup (ChainOrderTypes V)

/--
Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety of
groups? Here countable includes finite ordinals and zero.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal.{0}, α.card ≤ ℵ₀ → ∃ V : GroupVariety, ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»
modeling_decisions: A group variety is represented by its equational theory: a fully invariant normal subgroup of the free group on countably many generators. This is the standard Birkhoff/Neumann representation and avoids universe-dependent classes of all groups.
Subvariety inclusion is reverse strict inclusion of law subgroups: U is a proper subvariety of V exactly when V.laws < U.laws.
A well-ordered inclusion chain of order type o is represented by a strictly inclusion-increasing map from o.ToType, with every member a proper subvariety of the ambient variety.
Order types and ordinal height are pinned to Ordinal.{0}, matching the fixed small type of group varieties and avoiding irrelevant universe-lift artifacts.
Countability is expressed as α.card ≤ ℵ₀, which includes zero and all finite ordinals.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.26

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The ordinal height of a variety of groups is the supremum of the order types of all chains of
proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. Is every countable ordinal the ordinal
height of some variety?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Ordinal

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/-- A subgroup of the countably generated free group is fully invariant if every endomorphism
maps it into itself. -/
def IsFullyInvariant (N : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, N.map f ≤ N

/-- A variety of groups, represented by its equational theory in the free group on countably
many generators. Equational theories are fully invariant subgroups. The order is reversed because
a smaller variety satisfies more laws. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := OrderDual {N : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) // IsFullyInvariant N}

/-- A well-ordered-by-inclusion chain of proper subvarieties of `V`. -/
structure ProperSubvarietyChain (V : GroupVariety) where
  carrier : Set GroupVariety
  isProper : ∀ W ∈ carrier, W < V
  isWellOrder : IsWellOrder {W // W ∈ carrier} (fun W₁ W₂ => W₁.1 < W₂.1)

/-- The order type of a well-ordered chain of proper subvarieties. -/
noncomputable def ProperSubvarietyChain.orderType {V : GroupVariety}
    (C : ProperSubvarietyChain V) : Ordinal :=
  @Ordinal.type {W // W ∈ C.carrier} (fun W₁ W₂ => W₁.1 < W₂.1) C.isWellOrder

/-- The ordinal height of a variety is the supremum of the order types of all its
well-ordered-by-inclusion chains of proper subvarieties. -/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal :=
  ⨆ C : ProperSubvarietyChain V, C.orderType

/--
Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety of groups?
Here countable ordinals include all finite ordinals, including zero.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal, α < ω₁ → ∃ V : GroupVariety, ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»
modeling_decisions: A group variety is represented, via the standard Birkhoff–Neumann correspondence, by its equational theory: a fully invariant subgroup of the free group on countably many generators.
The order on equational theories is reversed, so the inherited order on `GroupVariety` is inclusion of the corresponding classes of groups.

A well-ordered chain is represented as a subset of the set-sized type of group varieties, with strict inclusion as its well-order relation; every member is required to be strictly below the ambient variety.
Ordinal height uses the ordinary ordinal indexed supremum `⨆`, not `Ordinal.lsub`, since the source asks for a supremum rather than a least strict upper bound.
Countable ordinals are expressed as `α < ω₁`, including zero and all finite ordinals. The `Ordinal` scope is explicitly opened so `ω₁` elaborates as the first uncountable ordinal.
